overall_assessment: The consumer contract suite and downstream canary architecture codified in integration/consumer-contract-suite.json, migration/sourceright/parity-cases.json, and .github/workflows/integration-release-train.yml provide an exemplary boundary separation between evidence producers and downstream consumers. The suite specifies 9 active cross-repository interactions, centrally featuring citeweft-to-searchright-document-evidence (edithatogo/citeweft -> edithatogo/searchright) and searchright-to-sourceright-shared-runtime (edithatogo/searchright -> edithatogo/sourceright). Every interaction strictly enforces distinct producer and consumer identities, explicit schema and contract versions, concrete fixture paths that exist on disk, executable verification gates, and fail-closed failure semantics. For CiteWeft, failure semantics dictate: Block CiteWeft pin promotion, keep the adapter optional and preserve raw extraction evidence for review. For Sourceright, failure semantics mandate: Do not cut over or delete Sourceright runtime code; retain dual-run and rollback paths. All 33 local file paths referenced across consumer contracts are verified to exist on disk by scripts/check_consumer_contracts.py. The integration CI workflow .github/workflows/integration-release-train.yml enforces read-only contents permissions and unpersisted credentials (persist-credentials: false), uploading read-only verification receipts with a 30-day retention window without performing unauthorized mutations.
verified_invariants: consumer contract interaction completeness: 9 structured interactions mapping producer contracts, consumer contracts, fixture paths, and executable gates
distinct producer and consumer identities: producer and consumer repositories are strictly distinct across all interactions
verified fixture paths on disk: all 33 local paths referenced in consumer-contract-suite.json exist and validate cleanly
fail-closed downstream canary failure semantics: failures block pin promotion, retain optional adapters, and forbid deletion of Sourceright runtime code
dual-run migration preservation: Sourceright runtime cutover is blocked pending dual-run parity verification against migration/sourceright/parity-cases.json
hardened CI workflow execution: .github/workflows/integration-release-train.yml restricts permissions to contents: read and uses persist-credentials: false

findings.description: Consumer contract suites and fixture definitions are fully specified in repository contracts; running compiler-backed consumer fixtures and live downstream canaries in CiteWeft and Sourceright CI environments remains an open operational gate.
findings.recommendation: Preserve open gate T32-G-DOWNSTREAM-CANARIES until downstream canary test runs execute against exact Searchright candidate pins.

findings.description: Failure semantics in searchright-to-sourceright-shared-runtime prevent premature removal of legacy runtime code, directly upholding the non-negotiable architectural rule that dual-run and rollback paths must remain available.
findings.recommendation: Ensure parity report receipts are generated and archived in verification/receipts/ prior to any future runtime deprecation.

assertions_evaluated.notes: Consumer contract suite, fixture paths, and downstream canary failure semantics verified in source contracts and deterministic test suites.
Producer-consumer interaction boundaries correctly preserve CiteWeft, Searchright, and Sourceright role segregation and promotion order.

limitations: Source-level validation of consumer contracts, fixture paths, and canary declarations only; execution of downstream canaries in remote repository pipelines remains an open gate.
